en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty Tenth Chapter
The Discussion on the Path for One Possessing the Fivefold Sense-Consciousness:
Is there cultivation of the path for one possessing the fivefold sense-consciousness? Yes.
Is it not the case that the fivefold sense-consciousnesses have arisen bases and arisen objects?
Yes, they do.
If the fivefold sense-consciousnesses have arisen bases and arisen objects, then indeed, it should not be said—
“There is development of the path for one possessing the fivefold sense-consciousness.
Is it not the case that the five sense-consciousnesses have pre-arisen bases, pre-arisen objects, internal bases, external objects,
unmixed bases, unmixed objects, diverse bases, and diverse objects, and do not constitute the range or domain of one another?
They are experienced; they do not arise without attention, nor do they arise without mental engagement, nor do they arise without being contiguous,
nor do they arise neither before nor after, nor do they arise one immediately after the other—
surely the fivefold sense-consciousnesses are effortless?
“Yes.

[The opponent asks: “If the five types of sensory consciousness are devoid of volitional effort (anābhoga), then surely it should not be said that ‘for one possessing the five types of sensory consciousness, there is the cultivation of the Path (maggabhāvanā).’”
Is there the cultivation of the Path for one possessing eye-consciousness? Yes.
Does eye-consciousness arise having emptiness as its object?
It should not be said thus...
[as before] ...Does eye-consciousness arise having emptiness as its object? Yes.
“Visual consciousness arises dependent on the eye and emptiness”?
One should not say so … [and so on] … “Visual consciousness arises dependent on the eye and emptiness”?
“Yes,” he said.
“Is there such a sutta as: ‘Dependent upon the eye and emptiness, eye-consciousness arises’?”
There is none.
Is there not indeed this sutta: “Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises”?
“Yes,” [you say].

But if there is indeed such a sutta as, “Dependent on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises,” then surely, O friend, you ought not to say: [that consciousness does not arise dependent on the eye and forms].
“Dependent upon the eye and emptiness, eye-consciousness arises.
Does one who possesses eye-consciousness possess the cultivation of the Path? Yes.
Does visual consciousness arise by taking as its object that which is past or future?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Does the cultivation of the Path exist for one who possesses visual consciousness?
“Yes.
Eye-consciousness arises conditioned by contact … conditioned by feeling … [and so on].
Taking perception as an object...
taking volition as an object...
taking consciousness as an object...
Taking the eye as a basis …pe… taking the body as a basis …pe… taking sound as a basis …pe…
Does it arise by taking tangible objects as its object?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Does one possessing mind-consciousness possess the cultivation of the Path, and does that mind-consciousness arise by taking emptiness as its object?
“Yes.
“Then for one possessing eye-consciousness there is the cultivation of the Path, and eye-consciousness arises having emptiness as its object?
“One should not speak thus…” [and so on].
It is admitted that for one possessing mind-consciousness there is the cultivation of the Path, and that mind-consciousness arises taking the past and future as its object.
Is it then admitted that for one possessing eye-consciousness there is the cultivation of the Path, and that eye-consciousness arises taking the past and future as its object?

It should not be said thus … [as before] … for one possessing mind-consciousness there is the cultivation of the Path, taking mind-consciousness as a condition for contact … taking feeling as a condition … [and so on].
Does it arise with reference to the tangible?
Yes. Does one possessing eye-consciousness possess the cultivation of the Path? Yes. Does eye-consciousness arise with reference to contact? Yes.
“Does [feeling] arise depending on feeling …pe… depending on the tangible?
One should not say so …pe….
Is it not to be said that "for one possessing the fivefold sense-consciousness, there is the cultivation of the Path"?
Yes, it is.
Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
"Here, monks, having seen a form with the eye, a monk does not grasp at its signs nor grasp at its secondary characteristics...
having heard a sound with the ear... and so forth?
“Having smelled an odor with the nose... pe...
having tasted a flavor with the tongue... pe...
having touched a tangible object with the body, one does not grasp at its signs nor grasp at its secondary characteristics.”
Is this indeed a sutta? Yes.
Therefore, it follows that for one possessing the fivefold sense-consciousness, there is the cultivation of the Path.
The discussion on the path for one possessing the fivefold consciousness is finished.
